Shipping Tools: Essential tools to streamline your shipping and logistics operations. Navaro provides calculators and document tools for freight and compliance, including CBM, duty, landed cost, export docs, and AI document checking.

CBM Calculator: Calculate cubic meters instantly for accurate shipping volume and freight cost estimation. Perfect for FCL and LCL shipments. Supports multiple units (m, cm, mm, in, ft) with automatic conversion. Get CBM calculations, volume weight, and container suggestions for 20 foot GP, 40 foot GP, and 40 foot HC containers.

CBM Calculator 3D: Visualize container packing with interactive 3D viewer. See how boxes fit in shipping containers. Real-time 3D visualization, rotate and zoom. Supports multiple container types with visual fill percentage. Export screenshots and CSV data for documentation.

Duty Calculation tool: Calculate import and export duties for multiple countries with HS code lookup. Includes GST, VAT, and other applicable taxes. Get detailed cost breakdowns: CIF value, duty amounts, total landed costs. Supports major trading countries. Find HS codes by product description and get duty rates.

Landed Cost Calculator: Calculate the total landed cost of imported goods accurately and plan your sell price. Includes product buy price, international freight, local import costs, customs duty per line, and VAT or GST. Helps businesses understand true product costs before shipping and avoid pricing errors. Available on the dashboard under Tools and from /tools/catalog. Tagline: Calculated landed cost and find your sell price — quickly determine landed cost and apply margins or markups to find your ideal sell price.

How to use the Landed Cost Calculator: Open the Navaro dashboard at /dashboard, go to Tools in the sidebar or quick-access cards, and select Landed Cost Calculator. You can also open it at /tools/catalog. Click Create New on the landing screen to open the full calculation form. The tool supports multiple product lines, live exchange rates, and instant recalculation of sell price when you change margin or markup.

Landed Cost Calculator inputs — Details section: Reference, Date, Country of Origin, Country of Destination, VAT or GST percentage, and Description. Transaction Details: Incoterms (EXW, FCA, CPT, CIP, DAP, DPU, DDP, FAS, FOB, CFR, CIF), Product Buy Currency, Final Local Currency, and Exchange Rate. Supported currencies: CAD, USD, EUR, GBP, INR, AUD. Exchange rate loads automatically from live rates API (/api/exchange-rates) when buy and local currencies differ; you can override manually. Freight and Import Costs: International Freight in USD (converted to final local currency), Local Import Costs in final local currency, and read-only Total combining both. Product Details table per line: Product Code, Description of Goods, Unit Type, Quantity, Buy Price per unit in product buy currency, auto-calculated Amount, Duty Rate percent, Cubic meters per unit, Cubic Total, Weight kg per unit, Total Weight kg. Add Line for more products; summary shows type count, total amount, cubic total, and weight total.

Landed Cost Calculator how it calculates: Freight and local import costs are allocated to each product line proportionally by line amount (quantity times buy price). Per unit: converted buy price (buy price times exchange rate), plus allocated freight costs, plus allocated import costs, plus duty amount. Duty is computed on converted buy price plus freight, times duty rate percent. Landed cost per unit equals converted buy plus freight plus import costs plus duty. Total landed cost equals landed cost per unit times quantity. Total tax equals total landed cost times VAT or GST percent. Click Calculate to show results. Disclaimer: calculator is a guide only — users must verify accuracy of landed cost.

Landed Cost Calculator results: Landed Cost table shows per product — buy price in product currency and final local currency, freight costs, import costs, duty amount, landed cost per unit, quantity, total landed cost, and total tax. Grand totals for total landed cost and total tax. Sell Price and Profit section: choose Margin percent or Markup percent per product line. Margin mode: sell price = landed cost divided by (1 minus margin percent over 100). Markup mode: sell price = landed cost times (1 plus markup percent over 100). Outputs sell price per unit, total sell price, profit per unit, total profit, plus average landed cost and portfolio totals. Results update live when margin, markup, or pricing mode changes after calculation.

Landed Cost Calculator vs Duty Calculation tool: The Duty tool estimates customs duties and taxes by country and HS code for import planning. The Landed Cost Calculator builds a full per-SKU cost model for a specific shipment — multiple products, freight allocation, local charges, exchange rates, duty per line, VAT or GST, and recommended sell prices with margin or markup. Use Duty for quick duty estimates; use Landed Cost when pricing inventory after a real purchase with known buy prices and freight bills.

Document Comparison tool: Compare specific fields between documents (BL Draft vs SI). Extract and compare shipping fields: Shipper, Consignee, Booking Number, Vessel, Ports, Container Number, Weight, HS Codes. Instant visual feedback on matches and mismatches with color-coded results. Verify shipping documents before shipment to avoid delays.

Navaro Templates: Bill of Exchange, Bill of Lading, Certificate of Origin, Certificate of Origin USMCA, CMR Carrier Consignee Sender, Request for Quotation, Sale Contract, Sale Invoice, Shipping Instruction. Download professional packing list and invoice templates for seamless documentation. Financial documents, shipping documents, certificates, CMR documents, business documents, contracts.
Bill of Lading is a shipping document that serves as a contract of carriage and receipt of goods. Used in ocean and multimodal freight.
Sale Invoice and commercial invoices are required for customs and payment. Packing lists detail contents of each package for customs and carriers.
Certificate of Origin certifies where goods were manufactured. Required by many countries for customs. USMCA certificate of origin for North American trade.
CMR is the international consignment note for road freight in Europe. CMR documents include sender, carrier, and consignee copies.

Shipping Resources: Comprehensive guides covering all aspects of shipping and logistics. Need help with a specific topic? Contact us. Categories: Shipping Basics, International Shipping, Cost Optimization.

Shipping Basics: Understanding shipping methods (Express 1-3 days, Standard 3-7 days, Economy 7-14 days), packaging best practices, labeling requirements, shipping insurance, tracking packages, handling returns. Use appropriate box sizes, padding, and secure closures. Learn the fundamentals of shipping, from choosing the right method to packaging your products correctly.
Common shipping methods include Express (1-3 days), Standard (3-7 days), and Economy (7-14 days). Choose based on your customer needs and budget.
Proper packaging protects your products during transit. Use appropriate box sizes, padding materials, and secure closures to prevent damage.

International Shipping: Customs documentation (commercial invoices, packing lists, certificates of origin), duty and tax calculation, import/export regulations, international carriers, prohibited items, HS code classification. Requirements vary by country and product type. Master international shipping with guides on customs, duties, regulations, and cross-border logistics.
Customs documentation typically includes commercial invoices, packing lists, and certificates of origin. Requirements vary by country and product type.
Duties and taxes are calculated based on the product value, origin country, and destination. Use HS codes to determine applicable rates.

Cost Optimization: Compare carriers (USPS, FedEx, UPS, DHL), rate negotiation, bulk shipping discounts, zone skipping, dimensional weight, shipping software. Strategies include volume discounts and optimizing package dimensions to avoid dimensional weight charges. Learn strategies to reduce shipping costs and optimize your logistics operations.
Compare rates across multiple carriers (USPS, FedEx, UPS, DHL) to find the best rates for your shipping volume and destinations.
Strategies include negotiating volume discounts, using zone skipping for long distances, and optimizing package dimensions to avoid dimensional weight charges.
